title: Why Your Drain Smells Like Sewer Gas
description: Sewer gas odors inside a building are often caused by a dried-out P-trap or a blocked plumbing vent. A P-trap holds a standing column of water that acts as a physical liquid seal, preventing volatile sewer gases from rising back up through the drain fixture. When a fixture goes unused for an extended period, evaporation depletes this water barrier. Alternatively, improper venting or a clogged roof vent can create negative pressure, pulling the water seal right out of the trap through siphonation. Regular fixture use, filling idle traps, and keeping roof vents clear preserve this critical protective barrier.
